This confirms `StartUpView.java` had the old no-arg signature since commit `148160d` (when `IPlayerClientListener` was introduced), and remained unchanged until `91aca37` changed the interface signature — breaking the build — which was only fixed later in `8225f5f`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 91aca3784a8d17eaa64cb298dae3cfb068efa8f4

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit adds a `Position` parameter to the overridden method `onUpdateCheckpointDirection()` in `StartUpView.java`, which strongly suggests an interface method signature was changed elsewhere without updating this implementer. I searched the history of `IPlayerClientListener.java` (the interface declaring this method) and found three commits touching it, with `91aca37` titled "player client: you can now pass the nextCheckpointPosition into the onUpdateCheckpointDirection method."

**(2) Specific change:** In `91aca37`, the interface method `IPlayerClientListener.onUpdateCheckpointDirection()` was changed to `onUpdateCheckpointDirection(Position position)`, and `PlayerClient.java`'s anonymous implementation was updated accordingly. However, `StartUpView.java`, which also implements `IPlayerClientListener` via an anonymous inner class, was not updated. Since `StartUpView.java`'s override still used `@Override public void onUpdateCheckpointDirection()` (no args), this became a compile error — `@Override` on a method that no longer matches any interface method signature.

**(3) Supporting evidence:**
- `git log` on `StartUpView.java` shows no commits between `91aca37` (the signature change) and `8225f5f` (the fix) — so nothing else could have caused or fixed this mismatch.
- `git show 148160d:...StartUpView.java` confirms the no-arg override existed since the interface was first introduced in `148160d`, consistent with it simply never being updated when `91aca37` changed the interface.
- The fix commit's diff exactly reverses the mismatch: it adds the `Position` import and changes the override signature to match what `91aca37` established in the interface.

I'm confident in this identification — the causal chain (interface changed in one file, implementer not updated, later fixed to match) is clear and directly evidenced by the diffs and file history.
